newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt down with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt down with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: A sharp selloff in both the U.S. Treasury market and stock market sent emerging market debt prices sharply lower, but market sources said trading volumes remained relatively thin.

"Surprisingly, it has been relatively quiet. There has been no panic considering what has transpired today," said one head emerging market debt trader at a major U.S. investment bank. "There have been no abnormal volumes."
At 1625 EST/2125 GMT, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was 1-18/32 lower, with the yield rising to 6.62 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 70.73 points at 6402.52.

Weakness in the U.S. Treasury market was triggered by comments in the Wall Street Journal today quoting Goldman Sachs International Vice Chairman Robert Hormats, who said he thought that the appetite for U.S. Treasuries by Japanese investors could wane.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television later this morning, Hormats elaborated, saying he did not expect "an enormous sea-change in Japanese investor thinking."

"Our market is following the Treasury market. There is clearly a growing change in sentiment," said another market source. However, he noted that the emerging debt market fell in tandem with U.S. Treasruies and did not widen against them.
At 1545 EST/2045 GMT, Argentine pars were 2-1/8 lower at 61-1/4 bid, while Mexican pars were 1-3/4 weaker at 71-7/8 bid and Brazil's "C" bonds were 1-5/8 softer at 71-5/8.
Elsewhere, Bulgarian debt continued to slip despite news that the IMF is expected to finalize talks with Bulgaria on a currency board early next year.
Bulgaria FLRB were 1-3/4 lower at 38-1/2 and its IABs were 1-5/8 weaker at 51-1/4.
